The estate and palace of the Marquis of Pombal, classified as a national monument, is an example of the valuable 18th-century heritage, designed by Carlos Mardel (a famous Hungarian architect).At the City Hall, also noteworthy are the pillory built in the third quarter of the 18th century and the 18th-century fountain with three spouts, designed by Carlos Mardel.Going up Rua 7 de Junho de 1759, we walk along an old street where Oeiras developed. At number 51, a prison once stood, and just there, on the left, you'll find a courtyard with two orange trees dominating the space.Continuing down the street and onto Rua Febus Moniz, you enter a pedestrianized street, where local businesses are the priority. To the east of the Parish Church is the Palácio do Egito Cultural Center.
